whatIsGprSurveying.headline: What is GPR Surveying?
whatIsGprSurveying.description: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is a non-destructive geophysical method used to detect and map subsurface features. SmartGrid Surveying utilizes advanced GPR systems such as the LMX200 to accurately identify underground utilities, voids, foundations, and anomalies without excavation.

gprLmx200.headline: GPR LMX 200
gprLmx200.description: Our LMX 200 will provide real time data as we scan through underground services such as electrical cables, PVC water line pipes, GI Pipes among others. Led By our surveyors, we further process the data after real time data is collected to provide comprehensive reports and maps that show the underground services networks mapped.

precisionBelowAndAbove.headline: Precision Below & Above
precisionBelowAndAbove.description: Smartgrid Surveying leads in Ground Penetrating Radar and Topographical Mapping -- Detecting the invidible and mapping the critical. High‑resolution subsurface scanning for utilities, voids, pavement assessments, and engineering investigations.

items.title: Utility Mapping – Nairobi CBD
items.description: Used: LMX200 Ground Penetrating Radar integrated with RTK-GNSS positioning. Objective: Detect and map existing underground utilities before foundation excavation. Result: Successfully identified fiber optics, power conduits, and storm drains — preventing costly conflicts during construction.

items.title: Pipeline Integrity Survey – Kisumu
items.description: Used: LMX200 GPR for non-destructive assessment of aging municipal water lines. Objective: Identify voids, pipe fractures, and leakage zones along the corridor. Result: Detected subsurface anomalies consistent with leakage and pipe deterioration, enabling targeted maintenance.

items.title: Archaeological Site Survey – Tharaka Nithi
items.description: Used: LMX200 GPR combined with drone-based topographical mapping. Objective: Locate buried cultural features without intrusive excavation. Result: Mapped subsurface stone alignments and structural remains while preserving site integrity.

items.title: Highway Expansion Risk Mapping – Nakuru
items.description: Used: LMX200 GPR in corridor scanning mode synchronized with GNSS data. Objective: Identify underground utilities and potential weak zones ahead of road widening works. Result: Provided high-resolution GPR profiles highlighting voids and buried services, improving design safety margins.

items.title: Industrial Site Clearance – Mombasa
items.description: Used: LMX200 Ground Penetrating Radar for pre-redevelopment clearance verification. Objective: Confirm absence of buried tanks, debris, or metallic hazards across a decommissioned port depot. Result: Verified the site as clear of subsurface obstructions, supporting safe redevelopment and compliance certification.
